question: Your developer productivity agent releases code through deploy_service, an MCP tool with an environment parameter. Policy requires an on-call engineer to approve each production release, but staging releases need no approval. Your team added a hook that intercepts every outgoing deploy_service call and redirects it to on-call approval. On-call engineers now receive dozens of staging requests each day, and these requests delay urgent production approvals. How should you change the hook?

options.text: Keep the hook redirecting every deploy_service call to approval, and add a second approval queue so that a separate group of engineers reviews all staging release requests each day.
options.reason: The hook still blocks staging releases that violate no policy; it should intercept and redirect only the policy-violating production releases.

options.text: Make the hook check the environment parameter of each intercepted deploy_service call, redirect only production releases to on-call approval, and let staging releases run.
options.reason: An interception hook should block only the actions that violate the policy and redirect them to the alternative workflow, so compliant staging releases can proceed.

options.text: Make the hook reject each production deploy_service call with an error message, and let staging deploy_service calls run without any approval step.
options.reason: The hook blocks production releases but sends them to no alternative workflow, so they never reach on-call approval; it should redirect them to that approval.

options.text: Remove the hook and add a system prompt rule that tells the agent to request on-call approval only before production releases of deploy_service.
options.reason: A prompt rule gives only probabilistic compliance, so the agent may still release to production without approval; the policy needs the deterministic guarantee of a hook.
